schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

260	## Action Items
261	
262	### A. Repo and safety (before any code)
263	1. [x] `git init` inside `vaani-ai-assignment`. The current git repository is the whole home folder.
264	2. [x] Add `.gitignore` with `.env`, `data/raw/`, `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`. Keep the Groq key only in `.env`.
265	3. [ ] Save `The_Relay_Assignment_Brief.pdf` into the repo.
266	4. [ ] Start exporting this assistant conversation as you go. It's a required submission item.
267	
268	### Schedule (author's decision, 2026-11-09)
269	
270	1. Probe first, in stages.
271	2. End of Day 1: exhaust the daily limit on a separate model the pipeline doesn't use.
272	3. Build the stand-in and the pipeline from the probe data.
273	4. Run the gold-set questions and the real load scenarios.
274	5. End of that day: exhaust the daily limit again, this time to collect the real "daily budget exhausted" scenario.
275	
276	**Risk to confirm on Day 1:** Groq reports a `reset-requests` duration, not a calendar reset. If the daily budget refills gradually over 24 hours instead of all at once, step 5 also eats into the next day's budget. Before step 5, read the reset behaviour from the Day 1 headers.
277	
278	**Model choice (author's decision, 2026-11-09):**
279	- Router: `openai/gpt-oss-20b`.
280	- Drafter: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Both have public prices, needed for cost per 1,000 answers.
281	- Sacrificial model for the Day 1 daily-limit test: `llama-3.1-8b-instant`. The pipeline doesn't use it.
282	- Accepted risk: the reasoning tokens gpt-oss produces may push back the first answer token. Probe phase 2 measures this. If it's too slow, `reasoning_effort` and the Llama models are the levers.
283	
284	### Phase 0 findings (Groq docs, read 2026-11-09)
285	
286	- **Free-tier numbers aren't public.** `console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits` shows only the Developer-plan table. Free-tier values are on the account's limits page in the console.
287	- **The headers cover only two limits.** `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` is RPD and `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens` is TPM. The `remaining-*` and `reset-*` headers follow the same split. `retry-after` (seconds) is sent only on a 429. **RPM and TPD aren't in the headers.** They come from the console or from hitting them.
288	- **Scope:** limits apply at the organisation level, and the table varies by model.
289	- **"Cached tokens do not count towards your rate limits."** Every probe prompt starts with a unique nonce to defeat caching.
290	- **Models:** the production text models are `llama-3.1-8b-instant`, `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` and `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Only the gpt-oss models list public prices ($0.075/$0.30 and $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens in/out). Those prices are needed for cost per 1,000 answers.
291	- **gpt-oss reasoning tokens:** these models reason before answering. The probe records the first reasoning token and the first answer token separately; the answer token is what users experience as time to first token.
292	- **Concurrency:** the docs don't mention a limit, so it is measured.
293	
294	### Probe findings so far (Day 1; recompute with `python -m probe.analyze_probe`)
295	
296	| Finding | Evidence (raw file: `results/probe_raw.jsonl`) | Confidence |
297	|---|---|---|
298	| `gpt-oss-20b`, `gpt-oss-120b` and `qwen3.8-27b` each allow RPD 1,000 and TPM 8,000. `allam-2-7b` allows RPD 7,000 and TPM 6,000. | `x-ratelimit-limit-*` headers | High |
299	| `llama-3.1-8b-instant` and `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` aren't available to this account. The Llama 8B call returned 404 `model_not_found`. | Probe record; `results/models_raw.json` | High |
300	| **The daily budget refills continuously; it doesn't reset at a fixed time.** `reset-requests` = requests used × 86,400/RPD exactly, at 1, 2, 17 and 32 used, and on 3 models. | Analyzer's "daily refill check" | High |
301	| **TPM refills continuously too.** 117 tokens used gave `reset-tokens` = 877 ms, versus 117/8,000 × 60 s = 878 ms. | Headers phase | High |
302	| `max_tokens` includes reasoning tokens. With `max_tokens=16`, `gpt-oss-120b` returned an **empty** answer. | Headers phase, `finish_reason=length` | High |
303	| With `reasoning_effort=low`, the reasoning cost is small: ~8 tokens (max 22). | Latency phase usage | High (n=45) |
304	| **Prompt size barely changes latency, but sets the budget.** Going from 264 to 2,813 prompt tokens added only ~200 ms to first-token p50 (492 → 696 ms), while using 10× the TPM. | Latency phase, `gpt-oss-120b` | Medium (n=15 per size) |
305	| **TPM is the binding limit.** At ~3K tokens per drafting call and TPM 8,000, `gpt-oss-120b` can serve about 2.7 drafts per minute, far below the RPM of 30. | Arithmetic on the measured limits | High |
306	| A large share of time to first token is spent waiting in Groq's queue: `queue_time` p50 300–370 ms against server compute of 290–430 ms. | Latency phase `usage.queue_time` | Medium |
307	| **Slow successes happen after the first token, as a trickle, not a stall.** On `gpt-oss-120b`, 3 of 45 requests in the first run and 2 of 30 in the instrumented rerun (6.7% in both) took 1.4–3.3 s *after* the first answer token. Groq's own `completion_time` for them was ≤ 0.28 s. In the instrumented rerun the longest silence was ≤ 347 ms: tokens arrived steadily at ~70 tokens/s against the ~476 Groq reports. Not seen on `gpt-oss-20b` (0 of 30). Groq-side or network-side is still unknown. | First run seq=5, 11, 15; rerun seq=2, 11 | Medium |
308	
309	| **RPM = 30.** The first 429 came at request #31, 13.0 s into a back-to-back burst. | `rpm_burst` | High |
310	| **A 429 identifies which limit was hit.** The body has `type: "requests"` or `"tokens"`, `code: "rate_limit_exceeded"`, and a message like "…on requests per minute (RPM): Limit 30, Used 30, Requested 1. Please try again in 2s." The `retry-after` header gives whole seconds, rounded up; the body gives the exact figure (e.g. "3.4125s"). | `rpm_burst`, `tpm_burst` 429 bodies | High |
311	| **A 429 is fast and free.** It returns in 51–59 ms, and `remaining-requests` didn't drop, so rejected calls don't count toward the daily limit. | Same records | High |
312	| **Recovery is quick: one bucket's worth of refill.** RPM recovered 2.0 s after the 429 (one request refills every 60/30 = 2 s). TPM recovered 4.0 s after (its deficit ÷ 133 tokens/s). There's no penalty period. | `*_recovery` records | High |
313	| **Groq reserves `max_tokens` against TPM before running a request.** The TPM 429 said "Requested 2876" = 2,812 prompt tokens + `max_tokens` 64. So an unused `max_tokens` allowance still uses budget. | `tpm_burst` 429 body | Medium–High (one 429; recheck on the daily run) |
314	| **No concurrency limit seen up to 16 requests at once.** 16 of 16 succeeded. In practice RPM and TPM cap concurrency long before any in-flight limit would. | `concurrency` | Medium (only tested to 16) |
315	| **Slowness is Groq-side queueing, and it comes in episodes.** In the 8-request batch, 5 of 8 waited 2.07–2.24 s in Groq's `queue_time` while server compute stayed at 125–142 ms. The 16-request batch, sent 30 s later, saw no such wait (max 642 ms). Requests sent together were delayed together, so the slowness is episodic and not caused by our concurrency. | `concurrency` level 8 vs 16 | Medium |
316	
317	**Design consequences:**
318	- **Set `max_tokens` tightly per step.** Router ~150, drafter ~600, with reasoning headroom. `max_tokens` is charged against TPM up front, so a draft with a 3K-token prompt and `max_tokens=1024` reserves ~4K tokens. That allows only ~2 drafts per minute.
319	- **Retry a per-minute 429 at the time the body states, not with blind backoff.** The precise figure is in the body; the header rounds it up. Never retry a 429 whose message says "per day".
320	- **Model slow episodes as correlated across requests.** In the stand-in, queue delay spikes should hit requests that arrive close together, not each request independently. Groq's `usage.queue_time` gives the real service's waiting-versus-working split for heading 4.
321	- **The load-slowdown curve can't be calibrated from the free tier.** No concurrency effect is visible up to 16, and RPM caps us at 30/min. The stand-in's slowdown under load is therefore assumed, not measured. This is "where it is least like the real thing" (heading 2).
322	- Retrieval size is limited by the token budget, not by latency. When the limit is close, reduce chunks fetched (k) first.
323	- The answer timeout splits into a first-token timeout and a total-time timeout. A silence timeout between stream events would **not** catch the trickle, because the stream never goes quiet. A slow trickle is mostly harmless to someone reading as it streams, so the total-time timeout should be generous.
324	- The stand-in models delivery as a mix: most requests stream at the server-reported rate, and ~7% trickle at ~70 tokens/s after the first token.
325	- Exhausting the drafting model's daily budget at end of day costs the next morning's budget: ~580 requests are back after 14 h.
326	
327	### B. Probe the real service (Day 1; log everything to `results/probe_raw.jsonl` via `python -m probe.groq_probe`)
328	1. [ ] Phase 0: read Groq's rate-limit docs and the console limits page for 2–3 candidate models.
329	2. [ ] Phase 1: one `max_tokens=1` call per model, capturing all `x-ratelimit-*` headers.
330	3. [ ] Phase 2: 60–100 streamed requests below RPM, at 3 input sizes (~200, ~1.5K, ~4K tokens), across 2 time windows. Gives first-token and total-time distributions.
331	4. [ ] Phase 3: RPM test. Send RPM+5 tiny requests within 10 s, then poll every 2 s. Records the 429 body, `retry-after`, and time to recover.
332	5. [ ] Phase 4: TPM test. Send ~4K-token prompts back to back until 429; confirm it is the token limit.
333	6. [ ] Phase 5: concurrency at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 parallel streams.
334	7. [ ] Phase 6: exhaust the daily limit on **one dedicated model not otherwise used**, near the end of a day, to see the real daily 429 and its reset.
335	8. [ ] Write a daily budget plan: how many real calls are spent on probes, retrieval evaluation and real load runs on each day.
336	
337	### C. Build
338	1. [ ] Ingestion: fetch the LaTeX sources at the exact versions, parse them into sections, chunk them into children with section paths, build the BM25 and embedding indexes.
339	2. [ ] Pipeline stages 0–6 with deadlines and cancellation.

| **TPM refills continuously too.** 117 tokens used gave `reset-tokens` = 877 ms, versus 117/8,000 × 60 s = 878 ms. | Headers phase | High |
| `max_tokens` includes reasoning tokens. With `max_tokens=16`, `gpt-oss-120b` returned an **empty** answer. | Headers phase, `finish_reason=length` | High |
| With `reasoning_effort=low`, the reasoning cost is small: ~8 tokens (max 22). | Latency phase usage | High (n=45) |
| **Prompt size barely changes latency, but sets the budget.** Going from 264 to 2,813 prompt tokens added only ~200 ms to first-token p50 (492 → 696 ms), while using 10× the TPM. | Latency phase, `gpt-oss-120b` | Medium (n=15 per size) |
| **TPM is the binding limit.** At ~3K tokens per drafting call and TPM 8,000, `gpt-oss-120b` can serve about 2.7 drafts per minute, far below the RPM of 30. | Arithmetic on the measured limits | High |
| A large share of time to first token is spent waiting in Groq's queue: `queue_time` p50 300–370 ms against server compute of 290–430 ms. | Latency phase `usage.queue_time` | Medium |
| **Slow successes happen after the first token, as a trickle, not a stall.** On `gpt-oss-120b`, 3 of 45 requests in the first run and 2 of 30 in the instrumented rerun (6.7% in both) took 1.4–3.3 s *after* the first answer token. Groq's own `completion_time` for them was ≤ 0.28 s. In the instrumented rerun the longest silence was ≤ 347 ms: tokens arrived steadily at ~70 tokens/s against the ~476 Groq reports. Not seen on `gpt-oss-20b` (0 of 30). Groq-side or network-side is still unknown. | First run seq=5, 11, 15; rerun seq=2, 11 | Medium |

| **RPM = 30.** The first 429 came at request #31, 13.0 s into a back-to-back burst. | `rpm_burst` | High |
| **A 429 identifies which limit was hit.** The body has `type: "requests"` or `"tokens"`, `code: "rate_limit_exceeded"`, and a message like "…on requests per minute (RPM): Limit 30, Used 30, Requested 1. Please try again in 2s." The `retry-after` header gives whole seconds, rounded up; the body gives the exact figure (e.g. "3.4125s"). | `rpm_burst`, `tpm_burst` 429 bodies | High |
| **A 429 is fast and free.** It returns in 51–59 ms, and `remaining-requests` didn't drop, so rejected calls don't count toward the daily limit. | Same records | High |
| **Recovery is quick: one bucket's worth of refill.** RPM recovered 2.0 s after the 429 (one request refills every 60/30 = 2 s). TPM recovered 4.0 s after (its deficit ÷ 133 tokens/s). There's no penalty period. | `*_recovery` records | High |
| **Groq reserves `max_tokens` against TPM before running a request.** The TPM 429 said "Requested 2876" = 2,812 prompt tokens + `max_tokens` 64. So an unused `max_tokens` allowance still uses budget. | `tpm_burst` 429 body | Medium–High (one 429; recheck on the daily run) |
| **No concurrency limit seen up to 16 requests at once.** 16 of 16 succeeded. In practice RPM and TPM cap concurrency long before any in-flight limit would. | `concurrency` | Medium (only tested to 16) |
| **Slowness is Groq-side queueing, and it comes in episodes.** In the 8-request batch, 5 of 8 waited 2.07–2.24 s in Groq's `queue_time` while server compute stayed at 125–142 ms. The 16-request batch, sent 30 s later, saw no such wait (max 642 ms). Requests sent together were delayed together, so the slowness is episodic and not caused by our concurrency. | `concurrency` level 8 vs 16 | Medium |

**Design consequences:**
- **Set `max_tokens` tightly per step.** Router ~150, drafter ~600, with reasoning headroom. `max_tokens` is charged against TPM up front, so a draft with a 3K-token prompt and `max_tokens=1024` reserves ~4K tokens. That allows only ~2 drafts per minute.
- **Retry a per-minute 429 at the time the body states, not with blind backoff.** The precise figure is in the body; the header rounds it up. Never retry a 429 whose message says "per day".
- **Model slow episodes as correlated across requests.** In the stand-in, queue delay spikes should hit requests that arrive close together, not each request independently. Groq's `usage.queue_time` gives the real service's waiting-versus-working split for heading 4.
- **The load-slowdown curve can't be calibrated from the free tier.** No concurrency effect is visible up to 16, and RPM caps us at 30/min. The stand-in's slowdown under load is therefore assumed, not measured. This is "where it is least like the real thing" (heading 2).
- Retrieval size is limited by the token budget, not by latency. When the limit is close, reduce chunks fetched (k) first.
- The answer timeout splits into a first-token timeout and a total-time timeout. A silence timeout between stream events would **not** catch the trickle, because the stream never goes quiet. A slow trickle is mostly harmless to someone reading as it streams, so the total-time timeout should be generous.
- The stand-in models delivery as a mix: most requests stream at the server-reported rate, and ~7% trickle at ~70 tokens/s after the first token.
- Exhausting the drafting model's daily budget at end of day costs the next morning's budget: ~580 requests are back after 14 h.

1. [ ] Phase 0: read Groq's rate-limit docs and the console limits page for 2–3 candidate models.
2. [ ] Phase 1: one `max_tokens=1` call per model, capturing all `x-ratelimit-*` headers.
3. [ ] Phase 2: 60–100 streamed requests below RPM, at 3 input sizes (~200, ~1.5K, ~4K tokens), across 2 time windows. Gives first-token and total-time distributions.
4. [ ] Phase 3: RPM test. Send RPM+5 tiny requests within 10 s, then poll every 2 s. Records the 429 body, `retry-after`, and time to recover.
5. [ ] Phase 4: TPM test. Send ~4K-token prompts back to back until 429; confirm it is the token limit.
6. [ ] Phase 5: concurrency at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 parallel streams.
7. [ ] Phase 6: exhaust the daily limit on **one dedicated model not otherwise used**, near the end of a day, to see the real daily 429 and its reset.
8. [ ] Write a daily budget plan: how many real calls are spent on probes, retrieval evaluation and real load runs on each day.

### C. Build
1. [ ] Ingestion: fetch the LaTeX sources at the exact versions, parse them into sections, chunk them into children with section paths, build the BM25 and embedding indexes.
2. [ ] Pipeline stages 0–6 with deadlines and cancellation.

# The Relay: Vaani take-home

A Python pipeline that answers engineers' questions using **only** three arXiv papers, on Groq's free tier. It must hold up under bursty load. A stand-in model service covers loads Groq can't take.

**The brief is the spec.** `The_Relay_Assignment_Brief.pdf` should be kept in the repo root. If it isn't there, ask the user for it. Check every plan against it, and point out anything it requires that we're skipping. The user wants this done strictly, without being asked.

**Design and decisions:** [docs/adr/0001-relay-pipeline-architecture.md](docs/adr/0001-relay-pipeline-architecture.md). Read it before you change the design. Add each new decision to it as it's made, with the date and who decided.

## Requirements checklist (condensed from the brief; the PDF wins if they differ)

- **Pipeline:** Python. ≥4 steps, ≥1 tool call, ≥1 branch or loop, and one step retrieves from the library.
- **Library:** arXiv 1706.03762**v7** (Attention), 2410.00037**v1** (Moshi), 2507.07955**v2** (Dynamic Chunking / H-Net), at exactly those versions.
  - Every answer cites where in the papers it came from.
  - If the papers don't say, the answer says so instead of guessing.
- **Stand-in service:** can be slow, fail, refuse at a limit, slow down under load, and stream. It is calibrated from real measurements, and the write-up says where it differs most from Groq.
- **Real probes first:** a modest number of requests to learn the latency spread, the limits, and the response at a limit.
- **Load runs:** ≥3 shapes. Table 2a requires 5 rows: steady, burst, sustained overload, per-minute limit halved, daily budget exhausted. Mark each row real or stand-in.
- **Answer quality:** at least 15 self-written questions, including some the papers don't answer. Report tokens per answer.
- **Retrieval:** at least 3 settings (piece size, pieces fetched, re-rank) with quality, tokens and first-token time. Pick one and say why. Say what retrieval does when the limit is close.
- **Raw file `results.csv`:** one row per request, with exactly these columns: `request_id, scenario, source (real|stand-in), start_time, first_token_ms, total_ms, status (ok|rate_limited|timeout|error), retries, tokens_in, tokens_out, retrieval_setting, answer_grade (correct|wrong|refused_correctly|refused_wrongly)`. **Every figure in every table must be computable from it.**
- **Tables:**
  - Table 1: limits, with value, how found and confidence.
  - Table 2a: latency, p50/p95/p99 for first token and total time.
  - Table 2b: outcomes, cost per 1,000 answers.
  - Table 3: retrieval settings.
  - Times in ms, percentages to one decimal place. Write "not measured" where something wasn't measured.
- **Write-up:** at most 2 pages, with these headings in this order:
  1. What I built and why
  2. The real service and my stand-in
  3. Results (include one number nobody could guess without running it)
  4. Where the time goes (waiting / working / retrying for one slow request; before or after the first token)
  5. When a limit is hit
  - **Retrieval: quality versus cost**
  - **How this library will mislead a naive retriever** (3 ways, each with an example question)
  6. Retries (the policy, plus one case where retrying made things worse)
  7. What the person sees (3pm, daily budget gone)
  8. Unsure / left out / learned
  - **Your feedback on Vaani** (vaani.dev)
  - **How I worked with the assistant**: the raw conversation history; the 3 prompts that mattered most; one thing the assistant got wrong that the user caught; one decision where the user overruled it; what in the submission is distinctly the user's
- **Ground rules:**
  - Submit within 4 days.
  - Never commit the key.
  - One free account. No tricks to get around limits.
  - The daily limit is shared across everything, so plan requests.

## Measured facts (Day 1, 2026-11-09; full table in the ADR; raw data in `results/probe_raw.jsonl`)

- **Models on this account:** `openai/gpt-oss-20b` is the router and `openai/gpt-oss-120b` the drafter. Each has RPD 1,000, TPM 8,000 and RPM 30. Llama models aren't available (404). The sacrificial model is `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, with the same limits.
- **Refill:** both the daily and the per-minute budgets refill **continuously**. Daily: one request per 86.4 s. Per-minute: 133 tokens per second.
- **`max_tokens` is charged against TPM up front**, and it includes reasoning tokens. Keep it tight. If it's too small, gpt-oss returns an empty answer.
- **A 429** returns in ~55 ms. The body's `error.type` is `requests` or `tokens`, and the message gives the exact wait. Rejected calls aren't counted.
- **Latency:** first answer token p50 ~0.5–0.7 s. Groq's `usage.queue_time` is often half or more of it, and it spikes in correlated episodes. About 7% of 120b responses trickle after the first token, at ~70 tokens/s.
- **Tokens per day:** not measured yet. It comes from the end-of-day daily test on qwen.

## Working rules

- **Never print, log or commit `GROQ_API_KEY`.** It lives only in `.env`, which is git-ignored. To check it, print its length and prefix only.
- **Every real Groq call costs shared daily budget.** Run `--dry-run` first, state the request and token cost, and get the user's OK before large runs. Don't exhaust a pipeline model's daily budget; it takes 24 h to refill fully.
- **Keep every raw result.** Append it; never overwrite `results/*.jsonl`. The reviewers will read them.
- **Calls about the design belong to the user.** Recommend, then record what they decide in the ADR. The user also has to report where they overruled the assistant, so don't quietly change a decision they made.
- **Environment:** Windows. Use `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (Python 3.11). Inline `python -c` with quotes breaks in PowerShell, so write a script file instead.

## Commands

```
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m probe.groq_probe --dry-run <phase> ...   # phases: headers latency rpm tpm concurrency daily
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m probe.analyze_probe [--model M]          # Table 1 + calibration numbers from the raw file
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m probe.list_models                        # models this key can use (not a chat call)
```

I've saved your paste and recorded it, and noted in the ADR that you kept the daily test for tonight.

**The console agrees with everything we measured.** RPM 30, RPD 1K and TPM 8K match the headers and the 429 messages. Most of Table 1 now has two independent sources each, which supports "High" confidence.

**It also shows a problem: tokens per day is 200K, and that's the daily limit that will actually stop us.**

- Today's probing already used about 82K of the 120b budget and 70K of the 20b budget.
- The quality evaluation the brief requires is at least 15 questions × at least 3 retrieval settings, so 45+ drafts or about 160K tokens. That's nearly a full day's budget by itself.
- The real load-run rows will need a day of their own.
- **So we need a daily budget plan before we build the evaluation or the load runs.** It decides which day spends tokens on what. I've marked it as blocking in the ADR (action item B8, the daily budget plan).

**It makes tonight's test simpler.** Using up 200K at about 7,600 tokens a minute takes roughly **26 minutes**. The test now checks the console figure and measures recovery, rather than discovering the limit.

If tokens refill the way requests do, at about 2.3 tokens a second, then after the limit is hit:
- a tiny request gets through after about 43 s;
- a full draft gets through after about 21 min.

That recovery is what Gap 3 is about.

**One decision before tonight:** should I add the recovery watching to the daily test? 1	"""Probe Groq's real service: how its latency is spread, what its limits are, and what it returns when one is hit.
2	
3	Every request is appended as one JSON line to results/probe_raw.jsonl. Each line keeps the full
4	response headers, the error body, Groq's own usage timings and our client-side timestamps,
5	so that Table 1 and the stand-in calibration can be recomputed from the raw file.
6	
7	Run from the repo root with the venv active. Always do --dry-run first; it sends nothing.
8	
9	  python -m probe.groq_probe headers     --models openai/gpt-oss-20b openai/gpt-oss-120b
10	  python -m probe.groq_probe latency     --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --per-size 15 --rpm 30 --tpm 8000
11	  python -m probe.groq_probe rpm         --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --burst 35
12	  python -m probe.groq_probe tpm         --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --size large --tpm 8000
13	  python -m probe.groq_probe concurrency --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --levels 1 2 4 8 16
14	  python -m probe.groq_probe daily       --model <sacrificial-model> --target tokens --confirm-exhaust
15	
16	The API key is read from .env (GROQ_API_KEY). It is never printed or logged.
17	"""
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import argparse
21	import asyncio
22	import json
23	import os
24	import random
25	import re
26	import sys
27	import time
28	import uuid
29	from datetime import datetime, timezone
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	import httpx
33	from dotenv import load_dotenv
34	
35	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
36	OUT = ROOT / "results" / "probe_raw.jsonl"
37	URL = "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions"
38	RUN_ID = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
39	
40	# Words of filler per size. One word is about 1.0-1.3 tokens; the real counts come from `usage`.
41	SIZES = {"tiny": 0, "small": 150, "medium": 1150, "large": 2700}
42	_WORDS = ("signal latency token budget queue retry window burst model stream paper section "
43	          "table figure encoder decoder attention chunk router limit replica shard cache").split()
44	
45	
46	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
47	def now_iso() -> str:
48	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")
49	
50	
51	def ms_since(t0: float) -> float:
52	    return round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)
53	
54	
55	def parse_duration_s(v: str | None) -> float | None:
56	    """Parse Groq reset/retry values: '7.66s', '2m59.56s', '1h2m3s', '120ms', or plain seconds '12'."""
57	    if not v:
58	        return None
59	    v = v.strip()
60	    try:
61	        return float(v)
62	    except ValueError:
63	        pass
64	    total, matched = 0.0, False
65	    for num, unit in re.findall(r"([\d.]+)(ms|h|m|s)", v):
66	        matched = True
67	        total += float(num) * {"h": 3600, "m": 60, "s": 1, "ms": 0.001}[unit]
68	    return total if matched else None
69	
70	
71	def build_messages(size: str, seed: int) -> list[dict]:
72	    """A unique nonce goes first in every prompt. Groq says cached tokens don't count toward limits,
73	    so a repeated prompt would make the latency and limit numbers look better than they are."""
74	    nonce = uuid.uuid4().hex
75	    rng = random.Random(seed)
76	    filler = " ".join(rng.choice(_WORDS) for _ in range(SIZES[size]))
77	    if size == "tiny":
78	        user = f"[{nonce}] Reply with the single word OK."
79	    else:
80	        user = (f"[{nonce}]\n{filler}\n\nIgnore the text above. In about 80 words, explain why an API "
81	                f"might limit requests per minute.")
82	    return [{"role": "user", "content": user}]
83	
84	
85	def is_gpt_oss(model: str) -> bool:
86	    return model.startswith("openai/gpt-oss")
87	
88	
89	def write(rec: dict) -> None:
90	    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
91	    with OUT.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
92	        f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
93	
94	
95	def classify_429(rec: dict) -> str | None:
96	    """Return which limit a 429 names, based on the error text (e.g. 'requests per minute')."""
97	    if rec.get("status_code") != 429:
98	        return None
99	    text = json.dumps(rec.get("error_body", "")).lower()
100	    for key, label in (("per day", "daily"), ("rpd", "daily"), ("tpd", "daily"),
101	                       ("per minute", "minute"), ("rpm", "minute"), ("tpm", "minute")):
102	        if key in text:
103	            return label
104	    return "unknown"
105	
106	
107	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- one request
108	class Prober:
109	    def __init__(self, key: str, reasoning_effort: str | None, dry_run: bool):
110	        self.key = key
111	        self.reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort
112	        self.dry_run = dry_run
113	        self.sent = 0
114	        self.client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(90.0, connect=10.0),
115	                                        limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=64))
116	
117	    async def close(self):
118	        await self.client.aclose()
119	
120	    async def call(self, *, phase: str, model: str, size: str, max_tokens: int,
121	                   stream: bool = True, meta: dict | None = None) -> dict:
122	        seed = random.randrange(1 << 30)
123	        body = {"model": model, "messages": build_messages(size, seed),
124	                "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "temperature": 0.2}
125	        if is_gpt_oss(model) and self.reasoning_effort:
126	            body["reasoning_effort"] = self.reasoning_effort
127	        rec: dict = {"run_id": RUN_ID, "probe_id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], "phase": phase,
128	                     "model": model, "size": size, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream,
129	                     "reasoning_effort": body.get("reasoning_effort"), "start_time": now_iso(),
130	                     **(meta or {})}
131	        if self.dry_run:
132	            rec["dry_run"] = True
133	            return rec
134	
135	        self.sent += 1
136	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
137	        first_reasoning = first_content = None
138	        chunks, parts = 0, []
139	        # Gap between consecutive SSE events; locates stalls in delivery after the first token
140	        last_event = None
141	        max_gap = max_gap_at = None
142	        try:
143	            async with self.client.stream("POST", URL, json=body,
144	                                          headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.key}"}) as r:
145	                rec["status_code"] = r.status_code
146	                rec["headers_ms"] = ms_since(t0)
147	                rec["headers"] = {k.lower(): v for k, v in r.headers.items()
148	                                  if k.lower() not in ("set-cookie",)}
149	                if r.status_code != 200:
150	                    raw = (await r.aread()).decode("utf-8", "replace")
151	                    try:
152	                        rec["error_body"] = json.loads(raw)
153	                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
154	                        rec["error_body"] = raw[:2000]
155	                elif stream:
156	                    async for line in r.aiter_lines():
157	                        if not line.startswith("data:"):
158	                            continue
159	                        data = line[5:].strip()
160	                        t_evt = ms_since(t0)
161	                        if last_event is not None and (max_gap is None or t_evt - last_event > max_gap):
162	                            max_gap, max_gap_at = round(t_evt - last_event, 1), last_event
163	                        last_event = t_evt
164	                        if data == "[DONE]":
165	                            break
166	                        chunk = json.loads(data)
167	                        if "error" in chunk:
168	                            rec["stream_error"] = chunk["error"]
169	                            break
170	                        for ch in chunk.get("choices") or []:
171	                            d = ch.get("delta") or {}
172	                            if d.get("reasoning") and first_reasoning is None:
173	                                first_reasoning = ms_since(t0)
174	                            if d.get("content"):
175	                                if first_content is None:
176	                                    first_content = ms_since(t0)
177	                                chunks += 1
178	                                parts.append(d["content"])
179	                            if ch.get("finish_reason"):
180	                                rec["finish_reason"] = ch["finish_reason"]
181	                        usage = chunk.get("usage") or (chunk.get("x_groq") or {}).get("usage")
182	                        if usage:
183	                            rec["usage"] = usage
184	                else:
185	                    payload = json.loads(await r.aread())
186	                    rec["usage"] = payload.get("usage")
187	                    msg = (payload.get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("message") or {}
188	                    parts.append(msg.get("content") or "")
189	                    rec["finish_reason"] = (payload.get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("finish_reason")
190	        except httpx.TimeoutException as e:
191	            rec["exception"] = f"timeout:{type(e).__name__}"
192	        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
193	            rec["exception"] = f"http:{type(e).__name__}:{e}"[:300]
194	        rec["total_ms"] = ms_since(t0)
195	        rec["first_reasoning_ms"] = first_reasoning
196	        rec["first_content_ms"] = first_content
197	        rec["content_chunks"] = chunks
198	        rec["max_event_gap_ms"] = max_gap          # longest silence between two SSE events
199	        rec["max_event_gap_after_ms"] = max_gap_at  # when that silence started, measured from send
200	        rec["output_preview"] = "".join(parts)[:160]
201	        rec["limit_hit"] = classify_429(rec)
202	        write(rec)
203	        return rec

206	def summary(rec: dict) -> str:
207	    h = rec.get("headers") or {}
208	    u = rec.get("usage") or {}
209	    return (f"[{rec['phase']}] {rec['model']} {rec['size']:<6} status={rec.get('status_code')} "
210	            f"ttft={rec.get('first_content_ms')} total={rec.get('total_ms')} "
211	            f"tok={u.get('prompt_tokens')}/{u.get('completion_tokens')} "
212	            f"rem_req(day)={h.get('x-ratelimit-remaining-requests')} "
213	            f"rem_tok(min)={h.get('x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens')} "
214	            f"retry_after={h.get('retry-after')} limit={rec.get('limit_hit')}")
215	
216	
217	def est_tokens(size: str, max_tokens: int) -> int:
218	    return int(SIZES[size] * 1.3) + 40 + max_tokens
219

221	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- phases
222	async def phase_headers(p: Prober, a) -> None:
223	    for m in a.models:
224	        rec = await p.call(phase="headers", model=m, size="tiny", max_tokens=16, stream=False)
225	        if p.dry_run:
226	            print(f"would send 1 tiny request to {m}")
227	            continue
228	        print(summary(rec))
229	        h = rec.get("headers") or {}
230	        print("   limit-requests (RPD):", h.get("x-ratelimit-limit-requests"),
231	              "| limit-tokens (TPM):", h.get("x-ratelimit-limit-tokens"),
232	              "| reset-requests:", h.get("x-ratelimit-reset-requests"),
233	              "| reset-tokens:", h.get("x-ratelimit-reset-tokens"))
234

236	async def phase_latency(p: Prober, a) -> None:
237	    """Sequential and paced below both RPM and TPM, so we measure latency, not queueing at a limit.
238	    Sizes are interleaved so that drift over time affects every size equally."""
239	    order = [s for _ in range(a.per_size) for s in a.sizes]
240	    rpm_gap = 60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety)
241	    if p.dry_run:
242	        toks = sum(est_tokens(s, a.max_tokens) for s in order)
243	        mins = sum(max(rpm_gap, est_tokens(s, a.max_tokens) / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60) for s in order) / 60
244	        print(f"would send {len(order)} streamed requests to {a.model}; ~{toks:,} tokens; ~{mins:.1f} min")
245	        return
246	    for i, size in enumerate(order):
247	        rec = await p.call(phase="latency", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=a.max_tokens,
248	                           meta={"seq": i})
249	        print(summary(rec))
250	        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
251	            wait = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after")) or 10
252	            print(f"   429 during latency phase; sleeping {wait:.1f}s (this sample is logged, not retried)")
253	            await asyncio.sleep(wait)
254	            continue
255	        used = (rec.get("usage") or {}).get("total_tokens") or est_tokens(size, a.max_tokens)
256	        await asyncio.sleep(max(rpm_gap, used / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60))
257

259	async def recovery_poll(p: Prober, a, model: str, size: str, max_tokens: int, phase: str, t_hit: float,
260	                        first_wait: float | None) -> None:
261	    """After a 429, wait for the retry-after hint, then poll until a request succeeds. Recovery time is
262	    measured from the first 429. Polls count toward RPM themselves, so the interval is kept coarse."""
263	    await asyncio.sleep(first_wait if first_wait is not None else a.poll_interval)
264	    for k in range(a.max_polls):
265	        rec = await p.call(phase=f"{phase}_recovery", model=model, size=size, max_tokens=max_tokens,
266	                           meta={"poll": k, "since_first_429_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t_hit) * 1000)})
267	        print(summary(rec))
268	        if rec.get("status_code") == 200:
269	            print(f"   recovered {rec['since_first_429_ms']} ms after the first 429 (poll {k})")
270	            return
271	        await asyncio.sleep(a.poll_interval)
272	    print("   did not recover within max polls")

275	async def phase_rpm(p: Prober, a) -> None:
276	    """Send tiny requests back to back, with no pacing, until a 429 or until `burst` requests have gone."""
277	    if p.dry_run:
278	        print(f"would send up to {a.burst} tiny requests back to back to {a.model}, then up to "
279	              f"{a.max_polls} recovery polls every {a.poll_interval}s")
280	        return
281	    t_start = time.perf_counter()
282	    for i in range(a.burst):
283	        rec = await p.call(phase="rpm_burst", model=a.model, size="tiny", max_tokens=8, stream=False,
284	                           meta={"seq": i, "since_burst_start_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t_start) * 1000)})
285	        print(summary(rec))
286	        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
287	            print(f"   first 429 at request #{i + 1} after {rec['since_burst_start_ms']} ms")
288	            ra = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after"))
289	            await recovery_poll(p, a, a.model, "tiny", 8, "rpm", time.perf_counter(), ra)
290	            return
291	    print(f"   no 429 after {a.burst} requests; RPM limit is above {a.burst} or the window is not 60s")
292	
293	
294	async def phase_tpm(p: Prober, a) -> None:
295	    """Send large prompts back to back until a 429 that names the token limit."""
296	    if p.dry_run:
297	        print(f"would send up to {a.max_requests} '{a.size}' requests (~{est_tokens(a.size, 64):,} tokens each) "
298	              f"back to back to {a.model}, then recovery polls of the same size")
299	        return
300	    for i in range(a.max_requests):
301	        rec = await p.call(phase="tpm_burst", model=a.model, size=a.size, max_tokens=64, stream=False,
302	                           meta={"seq": i})
303	        print(summary(rec))
304	        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
305	            ra = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after"))
306	            await recovery_poll(p, a, a.model, a.size, 64, "tpm", time.perf_counter(), ra)
307	            return
308	    print(f"   no 429 after {a.max_requests} requests")
309

311	async def phase_concurrency(p: Prober, a) -> None:
312	    """Fire N streamed requests at the same moment for each level, waiting `gap` seconds between levels so
313	    the per-minute limit doesn't confound the result. Watch whether latency rises or errors appear as N grows."""
314	    if p.dry_run:
315	        print(f"would send {sum(a.levels)} requests to {a.model} in levels {a.levels}, {a.gap}s apart")
316	        return
317	    for lvl in a.levels:
318	        recs = await asyncio.gather(*[
319	            p.call(phase="concurrency", model=a.model, size="small", max_tokens=128, meta={"level": lvl, "slot": j})
320	            for j in range(lvl)])
321	        ok = [r for r in recs if r.get("status_code") == 200]
322	        ttfts = sorted(r["first_content_ms"] for r in ok if r.get("first_content_ms"))
323	        print(f"level {lvl:>2}: ok={len(ok)}/{lvl} statuses={sorted({r.get('status_code') for r in recs}, key=str)} "
324	              f"ttft_min={ttfts[0] if ttfts else None} ttft_max={ttfts[-1] if ttfts else None}")
325	        await asyncio.sleep(a.gap)
326

328	async def phase_daily(p: Prober, a) -> None:
329	    """Run the model's daily budget down until a 429 that names a per-day limit. Paced just under the
330	    per-minute limits, so the 429 we get is the daily one. Use a model the pipeline does NOT use."""
331	    if not a.confirm_exhaust:
332	        sys.exit("refusing to run: pass --confirm-exhaust. This spends the whole daily budget of " + a.model)
333	    size = "tiny" if a.target == "requests" else "large"
334	    max_tokens = 8 if a.target == "requests" else 64
335	    gap = max(60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety), est_tokens(size, max_tokens) / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60)
336	    if p.dry_run:
337	        print(f"would send '{size}' requests to {a.model} every {gap:.1f}s until a daily 429 or "
338	              f"{a.max_minutes} min")
339	        return
340	    deadline = time.perf_counter() + a.max_minutes * 60
341	    i = 0
342	    while time.perf_counter() < deadline:
343	        rec = await p.call(phase=f"daily_{a.target}", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=max_tokens,
344	                           stream=False, meta={"seq": i})
345	        i += 1
346	        if i % 10 == 0 or rec.get("status_code") != 200:
347	            print(summary(rec))
348	        if rec.get("limit_hit") == "daily":
349	            print(f"   daily limit hit after {i} requests. Error body and reset headers are in {OUT}")
350	            return
351	        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
352	            await asyncio.sleep(parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after")) or 10)
353	            continue
354	        await asyncio.sleep(gap)
355	    print(f"   stopped at --max-minutes after {i} requests without a daily 429")
356

359	def main() -> None:
360	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
361	    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="print the plan; send nothing")
362	    ap.add_argument("--reasoning-effort", default="low", help="for gpt-oss models only; '' to omit")

376	    s = sub.add_parser("tpm"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
377	    s.add_argument("--size", default="large", choices=list(SIZES)); s.add_argument("--max-requests", type=int, default=6)
378	    s = sub.add_parser("concurrency"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
379	    s.add_argument("--levels", nargs="+", type=int, default=[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]); s.add_argument("--gap", type=float, default=30)

"""Probe Groq's real service: how its latency is spread, what its limits are, and what it returns when one is hit.

Every request is appended as one JSON line to results/probe_raw.jsonl. Each line keeps the full
response headers, the error body, Groq's own usage timings and our client-side timestamps,
so that Table 1 and the stand-in calibration can be recomputed from the raw file.

Run from the repo root with the venv active. Always do --dry-run first; it sends nothing.

  python -m probe.groq_probe headers     --models openai/gpt-oss-20b openai/gpt-oss-120b
  python -m probe.groq_probe latency     --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --per-size 15 --rpm 30 --tpm 8000
  python -m probe.groq_probe rpm         --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --burst 35
  python -m probe.groq_probe tpm         --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --size large --tpm 8000
  python -m probe.groq_probe concurrency --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --levels 1 2 4 8 16
  python -m probe.groq_probe daily       --model <sacrificial-model> --target tokens --confirm-exhaust

The API key is read from .env (GROQ_API_KEY). It is never printed or logged.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import random
import re
import sys
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from dotenv import load_dotenv

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "results" / "probe_raw.jsonl"
URL = "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions"
RUN_ID = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")

# Words of filler per size. One word is about 1.0-1.3 tokens; the real counts come from `usage`.
SIZES = {"tiny": 0, "small": 150, "medium": 1150, "large": 2700}
_WORDS = ("signal latency token budget queue retry window burst model stream paper section "
          "table figure encoder decoder attention chunk router limit replica shard cache").split()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")


def ms_since(t0: float) -> float:
    return round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)


def parse_duration_s(v: str | None) -> float | None:
    """Parse Groq reset/retry values: '7.66s', '2m59.56s', '1h2m3s', '120ms', or plain seconds '12'."""
    if not v:
        return None
    v = v.strip()
    try:
        return float(v)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    total, matched = 0.0, False
    for num, unit in re.findall(r"([\d.]+)(ms|h|m|s)", v):
        matched = True
        total += float(num) * {"h": 3600, "m": 60, "s": 1, "ms": 0.001}[unit]
    return total if matched else None


def build_messages(size: str, seed: int) -> list[dict]:
    """A unique nonce goes first in every prompt. Groq says cached tokens don't count toward limits,
    so a repeated prompt would make the latency and limit numbers look better than they are."""
    nonce = uuid.uuid4().hex
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    filler = " ".join(rng.choice(_WORDS) for _ in range(SIZES[size]))
    if size == "tiny":
        user = f"[{nonce}] Reply with the single word OK."
    else:
        user = (f"[{nonce}]\n{filler}\n\nIgnore the text above. In about 80 words, explain why an API "
                f"might limit requests per minute.")
    return [{"role": "user", "content": user}]


def is_gpt_oss(model: str) -> bool:
    return model.startswith("openai/gpt-oss")


def write(rec: dict) -> None:
    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with OUT.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def classify_429(rec: dict) -> str | None:
    """Return which limit a 429 names, based on the error text (e.g. 'requests per minute')."""
    if rec.get("status_code") != 429:
        return None
    text = json.dumps(rec.get("error_body", "")).lower()
    for key, label in (("per day", "daily"), ("rpd", "daily"), ("tpd", "daily"),
                       ("per minute", "minute"), ("rpm", "minute"), ("tpm", "minute")):
        if key in text:
            return label
    return "unknown"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- one request
class Prober:
    def __init__(self, key: str, reasoning_effort: str | None, dry_run: bool):
        self.key = key
        self.reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        self.sent = 0
        self.client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(90.0, connect=10.0),
                                        limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=64))

    async def close(self):
        await self.client.aclose()

    async def call(self, *, phase: str, model: str, size: str, max_tokens: int,
                   stream: bool = True, meta: dict | None = None) -> dict:
        seed = random.randrange(1 << 30)
        body = {"model": model, "messages": build_messages(size, seed),
                "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream, "temperature": 0.2}
        if is_gpt_oss(model) and self.reasoning_effort:
            body["reasoning_effort"] = self.reasoning_effort
        rec: dict = {"run_id": RUN_ID, "probe_id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:12], "phase": phase,
                     "model": model, "size": size, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "stream": stream,
                     "reasoning_effort": body.get("reasoning_effort"), "start_time": now_iso(),
                     **(meta or {})}
        if self.dry_run:
            rec["dry_run"] = True
            return rec

        self.sent += 1
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        first_reasoning = first_content = None
        chunks, parts = 0, []
        # Gap between consecutive SSE events; locates stalls in delivery after the first token
        last_event = None
        max_gap = max_gap_at = None
        try:
            async with self.client.stream("POST", URL, json=body,
                                          headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.key}"}) as r:
                rec["status_code"] = r.status_code
                rec["headers_ms"] = ms_since(t0)
                rec["headers"] = {k.lower(): v for k, v in r.headers.items()
                                  if k.lower() not in ("set-cookie",)}
                if r.status_code != 200:
                    raw = (await r.aread()).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                    try:
                        rec["error_body"] = json.loads(raw)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        rec["error_body"] = raw[:2000]
                elif stream:
                    async for line in r.aiter_lines():
                        if not line.startswith("data:"):
                            continue
                        data = line[5:].strip()
                        t_evt = ms_since(t0)
                        if last_event is not None and (max_gap is None or t_evt - last_event > max_gap):
                            max_gap, max_gap_at = round(t_evt - last_event, 1), last_event
                        last_event = t_evt
                        if data == "[DONE]":
                            break
                        chunk = json.loads(data)
                        if "error" in chunk:
                            rec["stream_error"] = chunk["error"]
                            break
                        for ch in chunk.get("choices") or []:
                            d = ch.get("delta") or {}
                            if d.get("reasoning") and first_reasoning is None:
                                first_reasoning = ms_since(t0)
                            if d.get("content"):
                                if first_content is None:
                                    first_content = ms_since(t0)
                                chunks += 1
                                parts.append(d["content"])
                            if ch.get("finish_reason"):
                                rec["finish_reason"] = ch["finish_reason"]
                        usage = chunk.get("usage") or (chunk.get("x_groq") or {}).get("usage")
                        if usage:
                            rec["usage"] = usage
                else:
                    payload = json.loads(await r.aread())
                    rec["usage"] = payload.get("usage")
                    msg = (payload.get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("message") or {}
                    parts.append(msg.get("content") or "")
                    rec["finish_reason"] = (payload.get("choices") or [{}])[0].get("finish_reason")
        except httpx.TimeoutException as e:
            rec["exception"] = f"timeout:{type(e).__name__}"
        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
            rec["exception"] = f"http:{type(e).__name__}:{e}"[:300]
        rec["total_ms"] = ms_since(t0)
        rec["first_reasoning_ms"] = first_reasoning
        rec["first_content_ms"] = first_content
        rec["content_chunks"] = chunks
        rec["max_event_gap_ms"] = max_gap          # longest silence between two SSE events
        rec["max_event_gap_after_ms"] = max_gap_at  # when that silence started, measured from send
        rec["output_preview"] = "".join(parts)[:160]
        rec["limit_hit"] = classify_429(rec)
        write(rec)
        return rec


def summary(rec: dict) -> str:
    h = rec.get("headers") or {}
    u = rec.get("usage") or {}
    return (f"[{rec['phase']}] {rec['model']} {rec['size']:<6} status={rec.get('status_code')} "
            f"ttft={rec.get('first_content_ms')} total={rec.get('total_ms')} "
            f"tok={u.get('prompt_tokens')}/{u.get('completion_tokens')} "
            f"rem_req(day)={h.get('x-ratelimit-remaining-requests')} "
            f"rem_tok(min)={h.get('x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens')} "
            f"retry_after={h.get('retry-after')} limit={rec.get('limit_hit')}")


def est_tokens(size: str, max_tokens: int) -> int:
    return int(SIZES[size] * 1.3) + 40 + max_tokens


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- phases
async def phase_headers(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    for m in a.models:
        rec = await p.call(phase="headers", model=m, size="tiny", max_tokens=16, stream=False)
        if p.dry_run:
            print(f"would send 1 tiny request to {m}")
            continue
        print(summary(rec))
        h = rec.get("headers") or {}
        print("   limit-requests (RPD):", h.get("x-ratelimit-limit-requests"),
              "| limit-tokens (TPM):", h.get("x-ratelimit-limit-tokens"),
              "| reset-requests:", h.get("x-ratelimit-reset-requests"),
              "| reset-tokens:", h.get("x-ratelimit-reset-tokens"))


async def phase_latency(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Sequential and paced below both RPM and TPM, so we measure latency, not queueing at a limit.
    Sizes are interleaved so that drift over time affects every size equally."""
    order = [s for _ in range(a.per_size) for s in a.sizes]
    rpm_gap = 60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety)
    if p.dry_run:
        toks = sum(est_tokens(s, a.max_tokens) for s in order)
        mins = sum(max(rpm_gap, est_tokens(s, a.max_tokens) / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60) for s in order) / 60
        print(f"would send {len(order)} streamed requests to {a.model}; ~{toks:,} tokens; ~{mins:.1f} min")
        return
    for i, size in enumerate(order):
        rec = await p.call(phase="latency", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=a.max_tokens,
                           meta={"seq": i})
        print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
            wait = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after")) or 10
            print(f"   429 during latency phase; sleeping {wait:.1f}s (this sample is logged, not retried)")
            await asyncio.sleep(wait)
            continue
        used = (rec.get("usage") or {}).get("total_tokens") or est_tokens(size, a.max_tokens)
        await asyncio.sleep(max(rpm_gap, used / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60))


async def recovery_poll(p: Prober, a, model: str, size: str, max_tokens: int, phase: str, t_hit: float,
                        first_wait: float | None) -> None:
    """After a 429, wait for the retry-after hint, then poll until a request succeeds. Recovery time is
    measured from the first 429. Polls count toward RPM themselves, so the interval is kept coarse."""
    await asyncio.sleep(first_wait if first_wait is not None else a.poll_interval)
    for k in range(a.max_polls):
        rec = await p.call(phase=f"{phase}_recovery", model=model, size=size, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                           meta={"poll": k, "since_first_429_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t_hit) * 1000)})
        print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("status_code") == 200:
            print(f"   recovered {rec['since_first_429_ms']} ms after the first 429 (poll {k})")
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(a.poll_interval)
    print("   did not recover within max polls")


async def phase_rpm(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Send tiny requests back to back, with no pacing, until a 429 or until `burst` requests have gone."""
    if p.dry_run:
        print(f"would send up to {a.burst} tiny requests back to back to {a.model}, then up to "
              f"{a.max_polls} recovery polls every {a.poll_interval}s")
        return
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    for i in range(a.burst):
        rec = await p.call(phase="rpm_burst", model=a.model, size="tiny", max_tokens=8, stream=False,
                           meta={"seq": i, "since_burst_start_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t_start) * 1000)})
        print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
            print(f"   first 429 at request #{i + 1} after {rec['since_burst_start_ms']} ms")
            ra = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after"))
            await recovery_poll(p, a, a.model, "tiny", 8, "rpm", time.perf_counter(), ra)
            return
    print(f"   no 429 after {a.burst} requests; RPM limit is above {a.burst} or the window is not 60s")


async def phase_tpm(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Send large prompts back to back until a 429 that names the token limit."""
    if p.dry_run:
        print(f"would send up to {a.max_requests} '{a.size}' requests (~{est_tokens(a.size, 64):,} tokens each) "
              f"back to back to {a.model}, then recovery polls of the same size")
        return
    for i in range(a.max_requests):
        rec = await p.call(phase="tpm_burst", model=a.model, size=a.size, max_tokens=64, stream=False,
                           meta={"seq": i})
        print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
            ra = parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after"))
            await recovery_poll(p, a, a.model, a.size, 64, "tpm", time.perf_counter(), ra)
            return
    print(f"   no 429 after {a.max_requests} requests")


async def phase_concurrency(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Fire N streamed requests at the same moment for each level, waiting `gap` seconds between levels so
    the per-minute limit doesn't confound the result. Watch whether latency rises or errors appear as N grows."""
    if p.dry_run:
        print(f"would send {sum(a.levels)} requests to {a.model} in levels {a.levels}, {a.gap}s apart")
        return
    for lvl in a.levels:
        recs = await asyncio.gather(*[
            p.call(phase="concurrency", model=a.model, size="small", max_tokens=128, meta={"level": lvl, "slot": j})
            for j in range(lvl)])
        ok = [r for r in recs if r.get("status_code") == 200]
        ttfts = sorted(r["first_content_ms"] for r in ok if r.get("first_content_ms"))
        print(f"level {lvl:>2}: ok={len(ok)}/{lvl} statuses={sorted({r.get('status_code') for r in recs}, key=str)} "
              f"ttft_min={ttfts[0] if ttfts else None} ttft_max={ttfts[-1] if ttfts else None}")
        await asyncio.sleep(a.gap)


async def phase_daily(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Run the model's daily budget down until a 429 that names a per-day limit. Paced just under the
    per-minute limits, so the 429 we get is the daily one. Use a model the pipeline does NOT use."""
    if not a.confirm_exhaust:
        sys.exit("refusing to run: pass --confirm-exhaust. This spends the whole daily budget of " + a.model)
    size = "tiny" if a.target == "requests" else "large"
    max_tokens = 8 if a.target == "requests" else 64
    gap = max(60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety), est_tokens(size, max_tokens) / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60)
    if p.dry_run:
        print(f"would send '{size}' requests to {a.model} every {gap:.1f}s until a daily 429 or "
              f"{a.max_minutes} min")
        return
    deadline = time.perf_counter() + a.max_minutes * 60
    i = 0
    while time.perf_counter() < deadline:
        rec = await p.call(phase=f"daily_{a.target}", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                           stream=False, meta={"seq": i})
        i += 1
        if i % 10 == 0 or rec.get("status_code") != 200:
            print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("limit_hit") == "daily":
            print(f"   daily limit hit after {i} requests. Error body and reset headers are in {OUT}")
            return
        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
            await asyncio.sleep(parse_duration_s((rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after")) or 10)
            continue
        await asyncio.sleep(gap)
    print(f"   stopped at --max-minutes after {i} requests without a daily 429")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- cli
def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="print the plan; send nothing")
    ap.add_argument("--reasoning-effort", default="low", help="for gpt-oss models only; '' to omit")
    ap.add_argument("--rpm", type=float, default=30, help="assumed requests/min, used for pacing")
    ap.add_argument("--tpm", type=float, default=8000, help="assumed tokens/min, used for pacing")
    ap.add_argument("--safety", type=float, default=0.8, help="pace at this fraction of rpm/tpm")
    ap.add_argument("--poll-interval", type=float, default=5.0)
    ap.add_argument("--max-polls", type=int, default=24)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="phase", required=True)

    s = sub.add_parser("headers"); s.add_argument("--models", nargs="+", required=True)
    s = sub.add_parser("latency"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--per-size", type=int, default=15)
    s.add_argument("--sizes", nargs="+", default=["small", "medium", "large"], choices=list(SIZES))
    s.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=200)
    s = sub.add_parser("rpm"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True); s.add_argument("--burst", type=int, default=35)
    s = sub.add_parser("tpm"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--size", default="large", choices=list(SIZES)); s.add_argument("--max-requests", type=int, default=6)
    s = sub.add_parser("concurrency"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--levels", nargs="+", type=int, default=[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]); s.add_argument("--gap", type=float, default=30)
    s = sub.add_parser("daily"); s.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--target", choices=["requests", "tokens"], default="tokens")
    s.add_argument("--max-minutes", type=float, default=120); s.add_argument("--confirm-exhaust", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    key = os.environ.get("GROQ_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not key and not a.dry_run:
        sys.exit("GROQ_API_KEY is empty. Put it in .env (never commit that file).")

    async def run():
        p = Prober(key, a.reasoning_effort or None, a.dry_run)
        try:
            await {"headers": phase_headers, "latency": phase_latency, "rpm": phase_rpm, "tpm": phase_tpm,
                   "concurrency": phase_concurrency, "daily": phase_daily}[a.phase](p, a)
        finally:
            await p.close()
            if not a.dry_run:
                print(f"\n{p.sent} requests sent; raw lines appended to {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)} (run {RUN_ID})")

    asyncio.run(run())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

MEASURED_PROMPT_TOKENS = {"tiny": 98, "large": 2813}


def watch_line(rec: dict) -> str:
    return (f"   +{rec.get('since_first_daily_429_ms', 0) / 1000:7.1f}s [{rec['phase']}/{rec.get('watch_stage')}] "
            f"{rec['size']:<5} status={rec.get('status_code')} limit={rec.get('limit_hit')} "
            f"used={rec.get('limit_used')} requested={rec.get('limit_requested')} "
            f"stated_wait={rec.get('stated_wait_s')}")


async def phase_daily(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Run the model's daily budget down until a 429 that names a per-day limit, then watch it come back.
    Use a model the pipeline does NOT use.

    1. Exhaust: requests paced just under the per-minute limits, so the 429 we get is the daily one.
       With --target tokens, every second request asks for one word with a large max_tokens. The daily 429's
       "Used N" then tells us whether the daily budget is charged max_tokens up front or actual output.
    2. Drain: after the first daily 429 there are usually still a few thousand tokens left, enough for small
       requests. Tiny requests use them up, so recovery is timed from a truly empty bucket.
    3. Watch: a large request every --watch-every seconds (or sooner, at the wait the last 429 stated), and a
       tiny one in between until a tiny gets through. Refused calls are free and each one's "Used N" is a reading
       of the bucket, so the readings give the refill rate. After --watch-minutes, poll every
       --slow-every-minutes, up to --watch-hours, so a fixed-time reset or a rolling 24 h window is caught too.
       Stops at the first large success.
    --check-model sends one tiny request to that model before and after, to show whether daily budgets are
    per model (its counter shouldn't move) or shared."""
    if not a.confirm_exhaust:
        sys.exit("refusing to run: pass --confirm-exhaust. This spends the whole daily budget of " + a.model)
    tokens = a.target == "tokens"
    size, base_mt = ("large", 64) if tokens else ("tiny", 8)
    min_gap = 60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety)

    def plan(i: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
        if tokens and a.reserve_test_tokens and i % 2 == 1:
            return "ok", a.reserve_test_tokens
        return "explain", base_mt

    def pace(charged: float) -> float:
        return max(min_gap, charged / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60)

    if p.dry_run:
        prompt = MEASURED_PROMPT_TOKENS[size]
        charges = [prompt + plan(i)[1] for i in range(2)]
        per_req = sum(charges) / 2
        n = int(a.expected_tpd / per_req) if tokens else int(a.expected_rpd)
        mins = n * sum(pace(c) for c in charges) / 2 / 60
        print(f"model {a.model}, target {a.target}, pacing at {a.safety:.0%} of RPM {a.rpm:g} / TPM {a.tpm:g}")
        print(f"1. exhaust: ~{n} '{size}' requests (if TPD={a.expected_tpd:,}), ~{mins:.0f} min, "
              f"~{n * per_req:,.0f} tokens charged (all of {a.model}'s daily budget)")
        if tokens and a.reserve_test_tokens:
            print(f"   every 2nd request: one-word reply with max_tokens={a.reserve_test_tokens} "
                  f"(reserved vs used differ by ~{a.reserve_test_tokens - 5} tokens each)")
        if tokens:
            print(f"2. drain: up to {a.drain_max} tiny requests ({min_gap:.1f}s apart) until a tiny gets a daily 429;"
                  f" spends only the leftover (< ~{prompt + base_mt:,} tokens)")
        close_polls = int(a.watch_minutes * 60 / a.watch_every)
        slow_polls = int(max(0, a.watch_hours * 60 - a.watch_minutes) / a.slow_every_minutes)
        print(f"3. watch: up to {close_polls} large + {close_polls} tiny polls in the first {a.watch_minutes:g} min, "
              f"then up to {slow_polls} of each every {a.slow_every_minutes:g} min, up to {a.watch_hours:g} h. "
              f"Refused polls cost nothing; at most one tiny and one large succeed (~{prompt + base_mt + 110:,} tokens)")
        if a.check_model:
            print(f"   plus 2 tiny requests to {a.check_model} (before and after), ~200 tokens of its budget")
        return

    if a.check_model:
        print(summary(await p.call(phase="daily_check_before", model=a.check_model, size="tiny", max_tokens=8,
                                   stream=False)))
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    deadline = t_start + a.max_minutes * 60
    i, hit = 0, None
    while time.perf_counter() < deadline:
        task, mt = plan(i)
        rec = await p.call(phase=f"daily_{a.target}", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=mt, stream=False,
                           task=task, meta={"seq": i, "since_daily_start_ms": ms_since(t_start)})
        i += 1
        if i % 10 == 0 or rec.get("status_code") != 200:
            print(summary(rec))
        if rec.get("limit_hit") == "daily":
            hit = rec
            break
        if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
            await asyncio.sleep(rec.get("stated_wait_s") or parse_duration_s(
                (rec.get("headers") or {}).get("retry-after")) or 10)
            continue
        prompt = (rec.get("usage") or {}).get("prompt_tokens") or est_tokens(size, 0)
        await asyncio.sleep(pace(prompt + mt))
    if hit is None:
        print(f"   stopped at --max-minutes after {i} requests without a daily 429")
        return
    t_hit = time.perf_counter()
    print(f"   daily limit hit after {i} requests, {(t_hit - t_start) / 60:.1f} min in.\n   message: "
          f"{error_message(hit)[:400]}")
    if a.check_model:
        print(summary(await p.call(phase="daily_check_after", model=a.check_model, size="tiny", max_tokens=8,
                                   stream=False)))
    await daily_watch(p, a, size, base_mt, t_hit, drain=tokens)


async def daily_watch(p: Prober, a, big_size: str, big_mt: int, t_hit: float, drain: bool) -> None:
    def el() -> float:
        return time.perf_counter() - t_hit

    def meta(stage: str, k: int, kind: str) -> dict:
        return {"watch_stage": stage, "poll": k, "kind": kind, "since_first_daily_429_ms": round(el() * 1000)}

    if drain:
        for k in range(a.drain_max):
            rec = await p.call(phase="daily_drain", model=a.model, size="tiny", max_tokens=8, stream=False,
                               meta=meta("drain", k, "tiny"))
            print(watch_line(rec))
            if rec.get("limit_hit") == "daily":
                print(f"   bucket empty: {k} tiny requests still got through after the large one was refused")
                break
            if rec.get("status_code") == 429:
                await asyncio.sleep(rec.get("stated_wait_s") or 2)
                continue
            await asyncio.sleep(60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety))
        else:
            print(f"   tiny requests still pass after {a.drain_max}; the watch starts with tokens left over")

    primary = "large" if big_size != "tiny" else "tiny"
    kinds = [primary] + (["tiny"] if primary == "large" else [])
    next_at = {"large": el() + a.watch_every, "tiny": el() + a.watch_every / 2}
    done: set[str] = set()
    k = 0
    while el() < a.watch_hours * 3600 and primary not in done:
        kind, t = min(((kd, next_at[kd]) for kd in kinds if kd not in done), key=lambda x: x[1])
        await asyncio.sleep(max(0.0, t - el()))
        stage = "close" if el() < a.watch_minutes * 60 else "slow"
        size, mt = (big_size, big_mt) if kind == "large" else ("tiny", 8)
        rec = await p.call(phase="daily_watch", model=a.model, size=size, max_tokens=mt, stream=False,
                           meta=meta(stage, k, kind))
        k += 1
        print(watch_line(rec))
        if rec.get("status_code") == 200:
            done.add(kind)
            print(f"   {kind} request succeeded {el():.0f}s after the first daily 429")
            continue
        step = a.watch_every if el() < a.watch_minutes * 60 else a.slow_every_minutes * 60
        stated = rec.get("stated_wait_s")
        # Probe again exactly when the 429 said to, if that's sooner: this checks whether the stated wait is true.
        next_at[kind] = el() + (min(step, stated + 1) if stated is not None else step)
    if primary not in done:
        print(f"   no {primary} request succeeded within {a.watch_hours:g} h")

async def phase_daily(p: Prober, a) -> None:
    """Run the model's daily budget down until a 429 that names a per-day limit, then watch it come back.
    Use a model the pipeline does NOT use.

    1. Exhaust: requests paced just under the per-minute limits, so the 429 we get is the daily one.
       With --target tokens, every second request asks for one word with a large max_tokens. The daily 429's
       "Used N" then tells us whether the daily budget is charged max_tokens up front or actual output.
    2. Drain: after the first daily 429 there are usually still a few thousand tokens left, enough for small
       requests. Tiny requests use them up, so recovery is timed from a truly empty bucket.
    3. Watch: a large request every --watch-every seconds (or sooner, at the wait the last 429 stated), and a
       tiny one in between until a tiny gets through. Refused calls are free and each one's "Used N" is a reading
       of the bucket, so the readings give the refill rate. After --watch-minutes, poll every
       --slow-every-minutes, up to --watch-hours, so a fixed-time reset or a rolling 24 h window is caught too.
       Stops at the first large success.
    --check-model sends one tiny request to that model before and after, to show whether daily budgets are
    per model (its counter shouldn't move) or shared."""
    if not a.confirm_exhaust:
        sys.exit("refusing to run: pass --confirm-exhaust. This spends the whole daily budget of " + a.model)
    tokens = a.target == "tokens"
    size, base_mt = ("large", 64) if tokens else ("tiny", 8)
    min_gap = 60.0 / (a.rpm * a.safety)

    def plan(i: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
        if tokens and a.reserve_test_tokens and i % 2 == 1:
            return "ok", a.reserve_test_tokens
        return "explain", base_mt

    def pace(charged: float) -> float:
        return max(min_gap, charged / (a.tpm * a.safety) * 60)

    if p.dry_run:
        prompt = MEASURED_PROMPT_TOKENS[size]
        charges = [prompt + plan(i)[1] for i in range(2)]
        per_req = sum(charges) / 2
        n = int(a.expected_tpd / per_req) if tokens else int(a.expected_rpd)
        mins = n * sum(pace(c) for c in charges) / 2 / 60
        print(f"model {a.model}, target {a.target}, pacing at {a.safety:.0%} of RPM {a.rpm:g} / TPM {a.tpm:g}")
        print(f"1. exhaust: ~{n} '{size}' requests (if TPD={a.expected_tpd:,}), ~{mins:.0f} min, "
              f"~{n * per_req:,.0f} tokens charged (all of {a.model}'s daily budget)")
